create.name: Cochise Zen Center
create.bio:
Cochise Zen Center is a small meditation community in Old Bisbee, in the borderlands of south-eastern Arizona. It began in 2003 as the Bisbee Lotus Sangha, a lay group loosely linked to Zen Desert Sangha in Tucson that kept up its practice for fourteen years without a resident teacher. In 2017 Zen Master Hye Mun (Barry Briggs), a Kwan Um School of Zen teacher who had led retreats across several continents and served as resident teacher at Cambridge Zen Center, retired to Bisbee; the following year the sangha invited him to be its guiding teacher, and it is now affiliated with the Kwan Um School.

The group meets in its own building on Brewery Avenue, a short walk up the hill from the Mimosa Market, and online. There are three sittings a week, on Sunday and Tuesday mornings in person and on Zoom and on Thursday evenings online only, with chanting and a short talk on Sundays. Longer Zen Days of alternating sitting and walking, public Dharma talks, occasional study workshops, private meetings with the teacher for kong-an practice and the two traditional Buddha festivals fill out the year. Everything is offered without charge, and practitioners from any tradition are welcome.

free_resources.title: Weekly Meditation
free_resources.description: Three group sittings a week: Sunday and Tuesday mornings at the centre and on Zoom, and Thursday evenings on Zoom, with chanting and a short teaching on Sundays. No charge; donations welcome.

free_resources.title: Zen Day, Dharma talks and workshops
free_resources.description: Regular half-day Zen Days of sitting and walking meditation, occasional public talks and study workshops with the guiding teacher, and the Buddha's Birthday and Enlightenment Day ceremonies, all free.

free_resources.title: Getting Started
free_resources.description: How to join a first sitting, with the offer of a short one-to-one orientation from the teacher or a senior student before practice.
